title: Unified span enrichment and dynamic burn-rate orchestration for SLO alerts
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: reduce noisy pager storms and improve root-cause signal by (1) enriching trace spans and log/metric contexts at the edge, and (2) evaluating burn-rate alerts with a dynamic orchestration layer that applies adaptive paging policies and anomaly scoring before escalation.

Background: Recent incidents (see incident-2024-11-07) showed that burn-rate alerts triggered broad pages without clear attribution; SREs spent >30m triaging missing correlation data. We need automated enrichment so traces/metrics/logs carry stable identifiers (route_id, model_variant, customer_tier, request_shape) and an orchestration component that scores burn-rate alerts for confidence and impact before paging.

Scope:
- Add lightweight span enrichment hooks for HTTP/gRPC frontends (Go/Node/Python SDK wrappers).
- Add a deterministic enrichment shim inside the inference runtime to stamp model_variant, sequence_length_bucket, and cache_hit tags into spans and emitted metrics.
- Extend the metrics/log pipeline to preserve these tags through aggregation (Prometheus -> remote_write + metric relabeling and Loki label retention for error logs).
- Build a burn-rate orchestration service that ingests alert signals, computes anomaly/confidence scores (baseline vs moving-window percentile + ML anomaly detector for high-signal routes), and applies policy decisions (suppress, route to silent SRE queue, route to paging).
- Add per-route paging policies: mute low-traffic routes, escalate high-traffic critical routes immediately, and support on-call round-robin for high-confidence outages.

Success metrics:
- Reduce duplicate/false-positive pages by 60% for inference-latency burn-rate alerts within 6 weeks of rollout.
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for SLO pages reduces by 25% due to better attribution in initial alert context.
- No increase in tail latency attributable to span enrichment (target <1% p95 overhead).
updates: 2025-02-12: Ticket created after post-incident retrospective; Asha wrote initial proposal and scoped dependencies.
2025-02-18: Design review with Observability and Runtime teams. Decided to implement enrichment in two layers: edge SDK + runtime shim. Runtime will be authoritative for model_variant tags.

2025-02-21: PoC of Go HTTP middleware implemented (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-sdk/pull/214). Middleware attaches span attributes: route_id, customer_tier, request_shape, sample_hint.

2025-02-25: Metric pipeline change drafted (Grafana Loki/Prometheus relabel rules) in config PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability-config/pull/58. Keeping high-cardinality labels limited to a white-list to avoid cardinality explosions.
2025-02-27: Burn-rate orchestration spec reviewed with SRE and Pager Duty owners. Agreed on three confidence bands: high (page), medium (silent SRE queue + slack alert), low (log only).

2025-03-01: ML anomaly detector prototype (historical baseline + EWMA residuals) integrated into orchestration service. Prototype code: https://github.com/redwood-inference/alert-orchestrator/pull/12.

2025-03-03: Engineering sync: runtime shim insertion point chosen in kv-cache commit path to guarantee stamp for requests that hit cache. Tradeoff: adds ~0.4ms to cache miss path; acceptable vs improved triage.

2025-03-04: Began canary rollout to non-critical routes (alpha customers) for the middleware and orchestration service. Monitoring dashboard created: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/Xz9s6/observability-orch (internal).
acceptance_criteria: Edge SDKs (Go/Node/Python) expose a standardized span enrichment API and are published as v0.2.0 with integration tests.
Runtime shim stamps model_variant, sequence_length_bucket, and cache_hit into spans and into metrics as labels; covered by unit + e2e tests.
Metric/log ingestion pipeline applies retention and relabel rules to prevent unbounded cardinality while preserving enrichment labels for top 200 routes.
Burn-rate orchestration service evaluates incoming alerts and routes them according to confidence band; manual override via Console feature flag must work.
Canary on non-critical routes ran for 72 hours with no customer-facing regressions; enrichment overhead measured <1% at p95 latency.
Documentation: Confluence runbook for SREs (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Span+Enrichment+and+Orchestration), and runbook steps added to oncall rotation page.
notes: Design trade-offs: We restrict enrichment to a curated label whitelist to limit cardinality. If customers require more granularity, we will expose a per-account opt-in config in a follow-up (ENG-32001).
Review feedback from Security (2025-02-24): Do not attach customer PII into spans. We added a sanitizer in the SDK to strip email/SSNs before enrichment.
Oncall experience: propose a new PagerDuty schedule for the 'inference-orch' service until we reach 2 weeks of stable runs, then merge into core SRE rota.
Fallback: orchestration will auto-fallback to original burn-rate alerting (legacy path) if enrichment metadata missing for >20% of incoming signals for a rolling 1h window.
Follow-ups: ENG-32002 (per-account enrichment settings), ENG-32110 (prometheus remote_write cost analysis), PM-512 (customer communication templates).
